metagame_characteristics.pace: Slower than modern metagames due to lack of Life Orb and other power items
metagame_characteristics.dominant_playstyle: Balance - teams that pose threats while maintaining solid defensive backbone
metagame_characteristics.key_mechanic: Spikes are the most important form of chip damage; no Stealth Rock exists
metagame_characteristics.weather: Sand Stream (Tyranitar) is dominant; Rain Dance teams are viable but require manual setup
metagame_characteristics.trapping: Dugtrio and Magneton are extremely common and shape teambuilding
metagame_characteristics.ko_ends_turn: When you KO a Pokemon, the turn ends completely - denying the opponent their turn. Use this to pivot into a trapper or disrupt the enemy and get a good pivot in.

clauses.sleep_clause: Only one opponent Pokemon may be asleep at a time
clauses.species_clause: No two Pokemon on a team may share a Pokedex number
clauses.ohko_clause: Fissure, Guillotine, Horn Drill, Sheer Cold are banned
clauses.evasion_clause: Double Team and Minimize are banned

unique_gen3_mechanics.explosion_self_destruct: Halves target's Defense during damage calculation (effectively doubles damage)
unique_gen3_mechanics.critical_hits: Ignore all stat changes (positive and negative), deal 2x damage
unique_gen3_mechanics.sleep_duration: 1-3 turns, not including the turn put to sleep
unique_gen3_mechanics.sandstorm_effect: Deals 1/16 HP damage per turn to non-Rock/Ground/Steel types. Note: The 1.5x SpD boost for Rock-types is a Gen 4+ mechanic and does NOT exist in Gen 3.
unique_gen3_mechanics.spikes_efficiency: Getting ONE layer of Spikes is the most efficient use. From 1 to 2 layers, you only go from 12.5% to 16.67% - that's only ~4% more damage for an entire turn. Prioritize getting Spikes up quickly over stacking layers.

S_tier.notes: Tyranitar is considered the best Pokemon in ADV OU. Skarmory is the best Spikes user. Blissey is the best special wall. Dugtrio enables many strategies through trapping.

A_tier.notes: Core metagame Pokemon that appear on most competitive teams

B_tier.notes: Strong Pokemon with specific roles or niches

C_tier.notes: Less common but have niches with proper support. Often need specific team support to shine.

tss_balance.name: TSS (Toxic, Sandstorm, Spikes) Balance
tss_balance.description: The quintessential ADV style featuring bulky Tyranitar, Spikes from Skarmory, and gradual chip damage
tss_balance.gameplan: Set up sand with Tyranitar, Spikes with Skarmory, chip down opponents with Toxic and forced switches

spikes_offense.name: Spikes Offense
spikes_offense.description: Aggressive teams that use Spikes to enable OHKOs and 2HKOs from offensive threats
spikes_offense.gameplan: Set up Spikes early, use trappers to remove key threats, clean with fast attackers. Spikes are critical for Dugtrio and Medicham to OHKO Tyranitar, Metagross, Swampert, and Celebi.

spikeless_offense.name: Spikeless Offense
spikeless_offense.description: Hyper-offensive teams that forgo Spikes for pure attacking power
spikeless_offense.gameplan: Overwhelm opponent with powerful attacks and momentum

breloom_charizard_offense.name: Breloom/Charizard Spikeless Offense
breloom_charizard_offense.description: Popularized by the player 'Undisputed'. This team gained so much traction that both Breloom and Charizard moved from UUBL to OU.
breloom_charizard_offense.gameplan: Breloom puts threats to sleep with Spore, Charizard wallbreaks TSS teams with Fire Blast. CM users like Celebi, Jirachi, and Raikou are staples.

superman.name: Superman (Anti-Spikes)
superman.description: Flying types and Levitate Pokemon all on one team to avoid Spikes damage entirely. Good matchup into Skarm/Bliss cores who rely heavily on Spikes chip to make progress.
superman.gameplan: Avoid all Spikes damage by using only Pokemon immune to them. Forces opponent's Spikes strategy to be less effective.

special_offense_dugtrio.name: Special Offense with Dugtrio
special_offense_dugtrio.description: Uses bulky Dugtrio to eliminate Blissey so special attackers like Suicune and Raikou can sweep. Zapdos/Dugtrio core is the backbone.
special_offense_dugtrio.gameplan: Trap and KO Blissey with Dugtrio, sweep with Crocune or CM Raikou. Can also run Rain offense variant.

stall.name: Spikes Stall
stall.description: Defensive teams relying on Spikes, status, and phazing to wear down opponents
stall.gameplan: Chip damage through Spikes/Roar/Whirlwind/Leech Seed, trap key threats with Dugtrio

rain_dance.name: Rain Dance
rain_dance.description: Weather-based offense using Swift Swim sweepers
rain_dance.gameplan: Set Rain Dance manually (no Damp Rock), sweep with boosted Water moves and Swift Swim
rain_dance.notes: Requires multiple Rain setters; strong vs standard offense, weak vs stall and Snorlax

milotic_celebi_balance.name: Milotic/Celebi Balance
milotic_celebi_balance.description: Alternative defensive core to SkarmBliss, relying on recovery moves
milotic_celebi_balance.gameplan: Use recovery to stay healthy, often paired with HP Fire Magneton and Claydol for Rapid Spin. Susceptible to chip from Spikes + Sand.

skarmbliss.description: The iconic defensive core - Skarmory handles physical attacks and sets Spikes, Blissey handles special attacks. Relies heavily on Spikes chip to make progress.

tyranitar_salamence.description: Dragon Dance sweepers that can clean games; Tyranitar's Sand Stream aids both
tyranitar_salamence.synergy: Both threaten different checks; Salamence's Intimidate helps Tyranitar set up

zapdos_swampert.description: Defensive pivots with good type synergy
zapdos_swampert.synergy: Zapdos absorbs Grass attacks for Swampert; Swampert absorbs Electric for Zapdos

zapdos_dugtrio.description: The backbone of special offense teams. Zapdos forces switches that Dugtrio can trap, particularly luring Blissey into Dugtrio's range.
zapdos_dugtrio.synergy: Use bulky Dugtrio to eliminate Blissey so special attackers (Suicune, Raikou) can sweep. Zapdos uses Baton Pass to bring in Dugtrio safely.
zapdos_dugtrio.strategy: Famously enables Crocune (CM/Rest/Sleep Talk Suicune) and Rain offense.

skarmdug.description: Skarmory sets Spikes, Dugtrio traps threats including Magneton
skarmdug.synergy: Dugtrio protects Skarmory from Magneton; Spikes enable Dugtrio's KOs

big_five.description: Classic balanced team core covering all major threats. Tyranitar provides Sand Stream, Skarmory sets Spikes, Swampert is the bulky pivot, Blissey handles special attacks, Gengar spinblocks.
big_five.notes: The 6th slot is flexible - often Celebi, Zapdos, or Dugtrio

magneton_crocune.description: Magneton traps and eliminates Skarmory, which is the main Pokemon that can Roar out Suicune. Once Skarmory is gone, Crocune (Rest/Sleep Talk Suicune) becomes nearly unstoppable as the last Pokemon.
magneton_crocune.strategy: Use Magneton early/mid-game to trap Skarmory. Save Suicune for last - nothing can phaze it if it's your last mon.

dugtrio.notes: Most versatile trapper; keeps many frail ground-weak Pokemon out of the tier. Key for special offense teams to eliminate Blissey.
dugtrio.common_set: Choice Band with Earthquake, Rock Slide, Aerial Ace, Hidden Power Bug
dugtrio.bulky_variant: Bulky Dugtrio for trapping Blissey on special offense teams

magneton.notes: Essential for teams weak to Steel-types; enables Dragon-types and Crocune

common_sets.hp_fire: Standard set for trapping Skarmory. Note: HP Fire requires imperfect Speed IV (30), making Magneton slower than max Speed variants.
common_sets.magnet_item: Magnet Magneton holds the Magnet item for boosted Thunderbolt power. More effective at eliminating Skarmory because Skarmory typically runs SpD EVs. Also stronger vs Metagross, Jirachi, and Forretress.
common_sets.endure_salac: After Salac boost, outspeeds entire OU except Jolteon/Aerodactyl - including Dugtrio.

counter_trapping.description: Double switching Dugtrio or your own Magneton to trap opposing Magneton
counter_trapping.yolo_skarm: Some Skarmory run HP Ground and max Speed to outrun HP Fire Magneton (which has suboptimal Speed IV). Not a great set but it exists.

spinblockers.description: Ghost-types that prevent Rapid Spin from removing Spikes. Critical for Spikes-based strategies.
spinblockers.why_essential: Spikes are the primary form of chip damage in ADV OU. If your opponent can freely spin, you lose the main way Spikes offense and stall teams make progress. Every Spikes team needs a spinblocker.

gengar.role: Primary spinblocker in OU. Offensive threat that can pressure spinners.
advantages: Levitate makes it immune to Spikes and Earthquake
STAB Shadow Ball threatens Starmie and Claydol
Can run offensive sets that threaten while spinblocking
disadvantages: Pursuit weak - Tyranitar can trap and KO
Dugtrio can trap non-Levitate variants (all Gengar have Levitate)

dusclops.role: Dedicated defensive spinblocker. Reliable but passive.
advantages: Much bulkier than Gengar - can take hits and stay in
Immune to Hi Jump Kick (from Medicham/Heracross)
Ghost typing makes it immune to Dugtrio's Arena Trap
Can support with Will-O-Wisp for physical attackers
Memento can support sweepers like Belly Drum Charizard

starmie.notes: Most common spinner. Fast, hits hard, has recovery. Gengar OHKOs with Thunderbolt.

claydol.notes: Bulkier than Starmie, immune to Thunderbolt. Weak to Shadow Ball. Often used on Balance teams.

forretress.notes: Can spin but is very passive. Rare in OU. Magneton traps it.

spinblockers.spinblock_priority: In most games, keeping your spinblocker healthy is a priority. Trade it only if you can secure a key KO or if Spikes are already doing their job.
spinblockers.importance: Without a spinblocker, opponents can freely use Starmie or Claydol to remove your Spikes - invalidating your entire chip damage strategy.

crocune.name: Crocune
crocune.creator: Cromat
crocune.set: Calm Mind / Surf / Rest / Sleep Talk
crocune.description: Great on Magneton teams because once Skarmory is eliminated, nothing can Roar Suicune out if it's the last Pokemon. Ultimate late-game wincon.

houdini.name: Houdini
houdini.origin: Named after a famous ladder player who always used a Metagross named Houdini
houdini.strategy: Lead Metagross with intent to use Explosion early. KO ends turn completely - denies opponent their turn. Use this to pivot into a trapper or get a favorable switch.

undisputed_offense.name: Undisputed's Breloom/Charizard Offense
undisputed_offense.impact: Both Breloom and Charizard moved from UUBL to OU because of this team's success

rock_resists.importance: Having multiple Rock resists is critical in ADV OU due to the prevalence of Tyranitar and Aerodactyl.
rock_resists.explanation: Rock Slide is extremely common - Tyranitar runs it on almost every set, and CB Aerodactyl's Rock Slide hits incredibly hard. If your only Rock resist gets trapped by Dugtrio or KO'd, you can lose to a simple Tyranitar sweep. Having 2-3 Rock resists ensures you always have a switchin.
rock_resists.synergy_note: Swampert, Metagross, and Flygon all resist Rock and complement each other - Flygon's Levitate avoids Earthquake that threatens the other two.

spinblocker_necessity.importance: If you use Spikes, you NEED a spinblocker. Without one, Starmie and Claydol freely remove your hazards.
spinblocker_necessity.explanation: Spikes are the backbone of ADV OU chip damage. Losing your Spikes means losing your primary way of wearing down switch-ins. Gengar is preferred for offensive teams (can threaten spinners), while Dusclops is better for stall (more reliable blocking, can support with Will-O-Wisp).
spinblocker_necessity.gengar_advantage: Gengar can OHKO Starmie with Thunderbolt and threatens Claydol with Shadow Ball. It also spinblocks while maintaining offensive pressure.
spinblocker_necessity.dusclops_advantage: Dusclops is bulkier and can't be trapped by Dugtrio due to its Ghost typing. It can support the team with Will-O-Wisp and Pain Split.

ground_immunity.importance: Having at least one Ground immunity helps handle Earthquake spam from Tyranitar, Swampert, and Dugtrio.
ground_immunity.explanation: Earthquake is the most common move in the tier. A Levitate user or Flying-type lets you switch into predicted Earthquakes safely and gain momentum.

status_absorbers.importance: Every team needs ways to handle Toxic and sleep.
status_absorbers.explanation: Toxic wears down your team quickly combined with Spikes and Sand. Rest/Sleep Talk Pokemon can absorb Toxic while remaining functional. For sleep, either lead with something expendable or use a Sleep Talk set.

dugtrio_proofing.importance: Dugtrio traps and KOs many key Pokemon. Building with Arena Trap in mind is essential.
solutions: Multiple targets so losing one isn't fatal
dugtrio_proofing.explanation: You can't always save a Pokemon from Dugtrio - but you can build so that losing one target doesn't lose the game. Having two Tyranitars' worth of value (e.g., Tyranitar + Aerodactyl for Rock-type offense) means Dugtrio can't cripple your gameplan by trapping one.

magneton_proofing.importance: If you rely on Skarmory for Spikes, you must have a plan for Magneton.
magneton_proofing.explanation: Magneton's Magnet Pull traps Skarmory and KOs it with Thunderbolt. Counter-trapping with your own Dugtrio is the most common solution. Some teams double up on Steels or run Forretress as a backup Spikes user.

electric_immunity.importance: Zapdos is omnipresent. Having a Ground-type or Electric immunity makes handling it much easier.
electric_immunity.explanation: Zapdos's Thunderbolt 2HKOs most of the tier. Ground-types are immune and can threaten back, while specially defensive Snorlax and Blissey can tank hits.

water_resist.importance: Starmie, Suicune, Swampert, and Milotic are common. Having answers to Water-types is crucial.
water_resist.explanation: Water-types have excellent neutral coverage. Grass-types like Celebi resist Water and threaten back, while bulky Water-types can check each other.
